start.text: Brenna's Goods. If it once had fur, teeth, or a pulse, put it on the counter and I'll name a fair price.

choices.label: Any advice before I go out?

buying.text: Pelts, mostly. Teeth if they're whole. Meat if you must — I'll salt it, I won't praise it.

advice.text: Buy a bandage before you buy a bigger axe. The road wolves are young. The pale ones by the northern rocks are not. Pride is expensive.

start.text: Frosthearth Inn. Stew's on, the beds complain, and the fire doesn't ask questions.

fall.text: You'll wake in my yard. I'll have words about the mud and none about how you got there. Try to come back walking.

stew.text: Turnips, salt, and a hope of mutton. It stays down. That's the whole recipe.

start.text: The fjord used to freeze clear to the skerries. A child could walk it. These days the ice argues back.

north.text: Wolves, not sailors. The young ones linger by the packed road. Further into the pines they run in pairs. The pale ones near the rocks can take a warrior apart.

hall.text: The hall is still a stack of timber and an argument. No trainer waits inside. Until the gathered families pick a master, the wilds will have to do the teaching.

start.text: Gate's open. Don't take that for a welcome from the wilds. Wolves have been crossing the packed road.

startTip.text: North, on the road, the young ones are bold and not very wise. If two of them look at you at once, walk back through my gate. The palisade is the end of their courage.

rule.text: The gathered families speak for Hoffender when they sit together. Between sittings I keep the gate, Hilda keeps the fire, and Brenna keeps the scales.
